title: Cohorted shadow siphon orchestrator for private control plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an orchestrator that performs cohorted shadow (traffic siphon) upgrades for private/VPC control planes using Terraform modules and an ops-side controller. The orchestrator must manage version pinning, cohort membership, siphon ratios, telemetry gating, automated rollback windows, and drift-safe Terraform operations.
background: Current private control plane upgrades are manual and rely on ad-hoc scripts. We need an automated, auditable process for customers on Private that minimizes blast radius during control plane version promotions while enabling deterministic rollback behavior and clear observability for health gating.
goals: Provide a Terraform-first orchestration flow for staged control plane upgrades
Support shadow traffic siphoning (0% -> mirror -> 50% -> 100%) per cohort
Automate telemetry-based gating and rollback triggers with configurable thresholds
Produce runbooks and preflight checks that reduce upgrade toil and failure modes
non_goals: Automatic in-place data migrations (outside control plane config changes)
Replacing platform-level customer scheduling policies (we will expose hooks instead)
proposed_solution: Create two Terraform modules (modules/controlplane/version_manager and modules/upgrade/traffic_siphon) and a small controller (go binary) that executes the staged plan. The controller will read a version manifest, create cohort groups via tenant filters, apply a siphon traffic-split config, run synthetic preflight probes, and evaluate telemetry signals (latency P99, error-rate, incoming request-rate, control-plane reconcile time). If telemetry breaches thresholds, open a rollback window and optionally perform an automated rollback via Terraform apply reversing the version_manager change.
tradeoffs: We add a controller that requires cluster permissions vs fully declarative Terraform-only flow; this simplifies runtime decisioning but increases attack surface and needs RBAC review.
Mirroring traffic for siphon cohorts can increase downstream load and cost; we will cap mirror rates and provide throttling knobs.
Automatic rollback reduces manual intervention but risks oscillation if signals are noisy; we will use consecutive-sample gating and cool-down periods.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules published to private-terraform-registry with clear inputs/outputs
Controller binary packaged and deployable to private control planes via customer operator or runbook
End-to-end e2e test: simulate cohort of 5 tenants, siphon 20% shadow traffic, detect synthetic probe failure and automatically reverse the version_manager terraform change
Documentation: upgrade playbook, operator RBAC manifest, and rollback runbook in Confluence
Security review completed and signed off by Security team

rollout_plan: Step 0: Feature-flagged deploy of controller to staging controlplane
Step 1: Publish Terraform modules to staging registry, run internal upgrade simulation
Step 2: Run shadow siphon against synthetic workloads with small cohort (10 test tenants) and observe for 24h
Step 3: Expand to 50 tenants and exercise telemetry gating and rollback paths
Step 4: Internal dry-run on customer-like staging clusters (with Ops participation)
Step 5: GA release for customers with opt-in and operator RBAC guidance
telemetry_signals: Control plane API 5xx rate (threshold: >0.5% sustained over 5m)
P99 request latency for data-plane requests proxied during siphon (threshold: >500ms)
Error spike in replication or worker queues (anomaly detection)
test_plan: Unit tests for Terraform module input validation
Integration test: controller toggles siphon feature and validates traffic-split via simulated requests
Chaos test: inject latency and errors in staging to validate automatic rollback
Security scan of controller binary and terraform module templates
Performance: ensure siphon controller adds <50ms median decision latency per upgrade step
rollback_policy: Automatic rollback when any critical telemetry signal breaching persists for 2 consecutive sampling windows
Manual rollback option with one-click revert in Console for Dedicated customers
Rollback window of 30 minutes after a stage change where automatic rollback is allowed; after window, action requires manual approval
Record all rollback decisions in audit logs and link Terraform state changes to the promoting PR
observability: Upgrade run timeline panel in Console showing stage, cohort size, siphon rate, and telemetry
Alerting rules that page SRE on rollback or failed apply (severity: P0)
Audit logs capture Terraform plan/apply diffs and controller decisions
Drilldown links to raw traces and sample request captures for failed cohorts
notes: We should coordinate with PM to determine default cohort sizes for new customers vs long-lived customers.
Evaluate whether mirror traffic should be compressed or sampled to reduce downstream cost.
Consider optional policy that drains mirrored requests to a debug sink to avoid affecting customer metrics.
